message.content: {"answer": "D", "option_text": "Left lung agenesis, supported by complete absence of left lung parenchyma and mediastinal shift to the left.", "reason": "The chest radiograph demonstrates complete opacification of the left hemithorax with ipsilateral mediastinal shift (trachea and heart shifted to the left) and elevation of the left hemidiaphragm. The right lung is hyperinflated and herniates across the midline. These findings indicate volume loss consistent with left lung agenesis rather than hypoplasia (which would show some residual lung tissue) or aplasia (which typically presents with a rudimentary bronchus but similar imaging; however, 'agenesis' is the standard descriptor for complete absence without airway remnant in this context). Option D correctly identifies the side and the supporting radiographic features."}
